# 1 Enoch Chapter 92 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 92:1 — Description of the book/writing

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "complete-wisdom-teaching of-this-instruction" | Literal compound; preserves Ge'ez mälkä sebet |
| LOGOS | "complete instruction of wisdom" | Formal; natural English word order |
| PNEUMA | "complete body of wisdom and instruction" | Expands for readability |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Complete instruction of wisdom' preserves both semantic elements without EMET's hyphenation or PNEUMA's expansion.

---

## 92:1 — 'praised by all men' vs. 'honored by all people'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "praised-by-all-men" | Literal; retains gendered 'men' |
| LOGOS | "praised by all men" | Formal; retains traditional rendering |
| PNEUMA | "honored by all people" | Gender-inclusive; 'honored' for 'praised' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'praised by all men.' The Ge'ez kuellu säb' does mean 'all people/humanity' but the traditional rendering is not misleading in context. 'Praised' preserves the specific connotation of public acclaim.

---

## 92:2 — 'spirit' vs. 'heart'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Let-not-your-spirit be-troubled" | Literal: ruh = spirit/breath |
| LOGOS | "Let not your spirit be troubled" | Formal; preserves 'spirit' |
| PNEUMA | "Don't let your heart be disturbed" | 'Heart' used for emotional seat in English |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET 'spirit.' The Ge'ez ruh specifies spirit/breath, not lebb (heart). PNEUMA's substitution, though emotionally natural, alters the precise term.

---

## 92:3 — 'lasting goodness' vs. 'eternal goodness' vs. 'bathed in lasting goodness'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "eternal-goodness and-grace" | Literal compound |
| LOGOS | "lasting goodness and grace" | 'Lasting' is natural; reserves 'eternal' for v. 4–5 |
| PNEUMA | "bathed in lasting goodness and grace" | 'Bathed' is vivid but interpolated |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Lasting' in v. 3, 'eternal' in v. 4, following the Ge'ez distinction. PNEUMA's 'bathed in' has no basis in the source.

---

## 92:4 — 'power' vs. 'authority'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "power" | Literal: hayil = strength/power |
| LOGOS | "authority" | Contextual; the endowment seems governance-related |
| PNEUMA | "power" | Agrees with EMET |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'authority' — in this eschatological context, hayil refers to the elevated status of the righteous, closer to delegated authority than raw strength.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 4**
